hypothesis: A factor-two target tile with 64 threads and 128 outputs per block preserves source-register reuse while changing CTA size and scheduling relative to the measured 128-thread factor-two candidate. Smaller per-CTA resource reservation may affect residency, but the effect is hardware-dependent; prior coarsened candidates were slower than baseline, so no speedup is assumed.
notes: This tests a launch-configuration change, not shared-memory source staging. The existing kernel bounds-checks both target indices, so partial tiles still cover each valid output once. The factor-two 256-thread parent was valid at 0.00272718 s and the factor-two 128-thread candidate was valid at 0.00261699 s; baseline was valid at 0.00184734 s. Register counts and occupancy data are unavailable here. The controller should run full correctness and official timing and measure this candidate before drawing conclusions.
transformations: Keep two output targets per thread, with the second target at threadIdx.x + blockDim.x, so each streamed source position and mass can be reused across both targets.
Set launch block size to 64 threads and items_per_block to 128; retain zero shared-memory allocation.
Retain per-target validity and self-interaction checks so arbitrary N and partial final tiles remain covered.
